Dear Hiring Manager,

I am applying for the Paralegal role at Montresor Legal supporting the international Funds practice. Although my background sits primarily in disputes and regulatory work rather than funds transactions, the core paralegal demands of the role, managing documents across a complex, deadline-driven matter, coordinating with multiple stakeholders and maintaining accurate case files, are ones I have handled directly and can bring immediately.

At BCLP I spent a year supporting live matters across two practice areas. In international arbitration I became the only junior on a complex investment arbitration shortly before a significant procedural deadline. I coordinated the outstanding document actions, tracked what was needed from the client, liaised with an external Romanian translator, and helped ensure the submission went out on time. That required me to hold the full picture of where a matter stood across multiple moving parts, which is the kind of organisation a transactional role with US-aligned deadlines will need. In real estate disputes I prepared electronic hearing bundles, assisted with court filings and managed large volumes of confidential documents across several concurrent matters. Both rotations gave me practical experience of the document-heavy, deadline-sensitive work that sits at the centre of a transactional paralegal role.

My more recent work at Citizens Advice has extended that into client-facing case management: I take instructions, draft correspondence, prepare document schedules and maintain confidential records across a wide range of matters. Working with clients on sensitive issues and translating complex procedural requirements into clear guidance has sharpened how I communicate across different audiences, which is relevant when coordinating between a London office and a New York team.

What draws me to this specific role is the international dimension. My LLM in Comparative and International Dispute Resolution gave me a grounding in how cross-border legal processes operate, and working on an investment arbitration involving Romanian-language materials gave me a practical sense of what international coordination actually involves. Supporting a transactional team working across jurisdictions and time zones is a direct extension of that experience, and the three-month contract is an opportunity to demonstrate what I can contribute in a funds context quickly.

I am available to discuss the role at short notice.

Yours sincerely,
Maria Silva

The paralegal role at Charlotte Tilbury is relevant to my background because, while my experience sits in disputes and regulatory matters, the core of paralegal work is consistent across sectors: managing documents and deadlines carefully, drafting clearly, and supporting a legal team under pressure. I want to work in-house because I am interested in how legal work connects to the commercial decisions a business is actually making, rather than arriving after a dispute has already started.
